newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Van Miert says concerned about UK digital TV plan. [CORRECTED 17:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Van Miert says concerned about UK digital TV plan. [CORRECTED 17:54 GMT]

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Tuesday he was concerned about plans to grant licences to operate digital terrestrial pay-television in Britain.

Van Miert told reporters the Commission had been asked by the British authorities to comment on the issue. He particularly singled out a bid by a group including British Sky Broadcasting and Carlton Communications.

He said earlier at a conference organised by the Wall Street Journal Europe that the plan was likely "to enhance the strong position" of some British TV operators and he believed such concerns were shared by the British authorities.
UK broadcasting regulator Independent Television Commission is expected to award three licences by the end of the month to run digital terrestrial television.
The project will give viewers the choice of 30 to 40 channels when it is launched by mid 1998.
(Corrects number of channels from "more than 200" to "30 to 40" and corrects launch date from late to mid 1998.)
BSkyB together with leading commercial TV companies Carlton and Granada Group have created a consortium called British Digital Broacasting (BDB) to bid for all licences.
BDB's only rival in the licence bid is Digital Television Network, owned by cable and transmission company NTL Inc .
